title: Guidelines on the Use of Therapeutic Apheresis in Clinical Practice-Evidence-Based Approach From the Writing Committee of the American Society for Apheresis: The Tenth Special Issue.
authors: Zantek ND, Alquist CR, Hofmann JC, Klingel R, Levenbrown Y, Onwuemene OA, Patidar G, Patriquin CJ, Raval JS, Sanchez AP, Schneiderman J, Tanhehco YC, Connelly-Smith L.

title: Aptamer-CRISPR/Cas as a tool in point-of-care testing of infectious diseases.
authors: Lau CH, Huang Y, Ch'ng ES, Tang TH, Zhu H, Citartan M
abstract: Aptamers and the CRISPR/Cas system have become the cornerstones of target detections due to their numerous advantages. Aptamers enable direct recognition of non-nucleic acid targets, such as pathogens and antigens, while CRISPR/Cas system drives signal amplification and rapid detection. The combined aptamer-CRISPR/Cas system can overcome the limitations of traditional target detection by realizing field-deployable, highly sensitive, specific, versatile, and rapid assays. Given the increasing number of different aptamer-CRISPR/Cas systems developed recently, particularly for infectious diseases, we provide a comprehensive overview of these platforms designed for detecting significant viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, Monkeypox virus, Hepatitis B virus and bacteria that include Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella. Current challenges that impede the deployment of aptamer-CRISPR/Cas for point-of-care pathogen detection were also mapped, including primary barriers such as clinical matrix effect and stability. Several strategies to mitigate these issues were also set forth, predominantly the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning to accelerate the transition of aptamer-CRISPR/Cas system to the clinical translation and commercialization phase, paving the way towards widespread implementation in global health.

title: Ultrasound-triggered bio-scaffold integrating engineered stem cells for cartilage regeneration.
authors: Guo J, Peng Y, Xiao X, Li S, Zhu J, Lin J, Li J, Wu D
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of the tissue and the poor therapeutic efficacy of current treatments. Although stem cell-based therapies hold promise, their clinical outcomes are often compromised by insufficient chondrogenic differentiation, phenotypic instability, and rapid cell loss in the dynamic joint environment. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive, bio-scaffold system (e-BMSCs/Gel) designed to enhance cartilage regeneration through coordinated biochemical and genetic regulation. In this system, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are engineered by internalizing nanobubbles (NBs) loaded with TGF-β3 protein and CRISPR/Cas9 plasmids targeting the YAP (pCas9-YAP), termed T@NBspDNA. Additionally, to enhance cell retention and survival, engineered BMSCs (e-BMSCs) are encapsulated within a thermosensitive thiolated-chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel that rapidly forms in situ. Under US stimulation, the synchronized activation of TGF-β3 release and YAP gene silencing significantly promoted the chondrogenic differentiation of e-BMSCs. Furthermore, in vivo evaluation in a rat articular cartilage defect model demonstrates that US-activated e-BMSCs/Gel effectively promotes hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and improves structural restoration of the defect site. Overall, this work presents a controllable bio-scaffold platform, offering a novel strategy for effective cartilage regeneration.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: Polymeric and metallic occluders for interventional therapy of cardiovascular diseases.
authors: Liu R, Wang Q, Ding J
abstract: Interventional therapy has, as a minimally invasive approach, been widely adopted for treating cardiovascular diseases, particularly structural heart disease, where occluders play a pivotal role in transcatheter closure. This paper comprehensively reviews the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of cardiovascular occluders, beginning with their interventional applications in congenital heart defects (atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent foramen ovale, and patent ductus arteriosus) and left atrial appendage closure. The focus then shifts to occluder materials and design principles, tracing the progression from early non-degradable metals like stainless steel to the current gold standard, nitinol, whose hyperelasticity enables self-expanding devices. To promote rapid endothelialization on nitinol implants, surface nanocoatings of bioceramics such as titanium nitride have been developed to modulate cell-material interactions. To eliminate risks from permanent metallic implants, biodegradable occluders have emerged as an alternative. The design of biodegradable occluders utilizing medical polymers such as polylactic acid and polydioxanone is illustrated, highlighting structural innovations such as locking strategies to overcome the lack of hyperelasticity. Key considerations including matching degradation rate with tissue regeneration and achieving X-ray visibility are also described. Finally, future perspectives are presented: expanding applications to infants and the elderly, incorporating tissue engineering for in situ regeneration, and leveraging nanotechnology and artificial intelligence to optimize device performance. The ongoing advancement of occluder technologies will propel interventional therapy for structural heart disease toward a safer and more effective treatment.

title: From biomarkers to therapeutic targets: Biomaterial-mediated cfDNA scavenging in inflammation.
authors: Liu S, Cheng X, Liu L, Luo E, Shao D, Huang H, Liu H
abstract: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) displays disease-dependent changes in abundance, fragmentation, composition, and tissue origin. Beyond serving as a noninvasive biomarker, persistent cfDNA can act as a damage-associated molecular pattern, activating TLR9, cGAS-STING, inflammasome signaling, and thromboinflammation. This review synthesizes advances in cfDNA biology, clinical applications, and therapeutic scavenging across inflammatory diseases. We critically evaluate the extent to which current clinical studies support diagnostic, prognostic, and causal conclusions while considering methodological heterogeneity. Particular emphasis is placed on how biomaterials transform cfDNA recognition into treatment. We trace the evolution from free nucleases and soluble cationic agents to nanostructured platforms that integrate DNA sequestration with retention, degradation, lesion targeting, or immunomodulation. Comparison of cationic polymers, dendrimers, core-shell nanoparticles, hydrogels, microneedles, nanosheets, and nuclease-enabled systems reveals how material architecture governs cfDNA accessibility, stability in biofluids, tissue distribution, and therapeutic efficacy. Localized and stimuli-responsive designs may improve selectivity and reduce systemic toxicity, but most efficacy evidence remains preclinical. Clinical translation therefore requires standardized cfDNA measurement, realistic biofluid testing, rigorous pharmacology, scalable manufacturing, and prospective demonstration that selective cfDNA removal improves outcomes without compromising host defense.

title: Engineering biomaterials to improve cytokine therapies for wound healing.
authors: Horton I, Maisel K, Sadtler K
abstract: Recombinant cytokines have been used as therapeutics for cancers, autoimmune diseases, and infectious diseases, but their application in wound healing and tissue regeneration remains relatively underdeveloped. Short half-lives, narrow therapeutic windows, and a myriad of adverse effects due to pleiotropy and redundancy have limited their clinical use. Biomaterial-based delivery platforms such as hydrogels, particles, and scaffolds have gained traction as engineering strategies to bridge this translational gap. Despite their popularity in preclinical research, the last FDA approved biomaterial-based cytokine therapeutic, becaplermin, was approved in 1997. Unlike reviews that focus on material design alone, we investigate clinical trials from 2012 to present day and look at the barriers and bottlenecks of translating this technology beyond the bench. This review focuses on release kinetics, design parameters, and practical applications of cytokine-loaded hydrogels, particles, and scaffolds to accelerate wound healing and regenerate functional tissue after soft tissue damage. We offer insights about future directions for preclinical testing and further engineering considerations to aid in their translation to clinical care for patients with soft tissue injuries.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit for highly sensitive detection of aflatoxin B1.
authors: Wu Z, Ma Y, Li X, Yan Z, Huang Y, Wang K, Quan W, Mo L
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic mycotoxin and strongly carcinogenic and teratogenic to humans. Achieving CRISPR-based sensing system for highly sensitive detection of AFB1 remains a significant challenge. A CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit (CPSCN) is proposed for the sensitive and accurate detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). In the CPSCN sensing system, CRISPR/Cas12a/gRNA1 indirectly recognizes AFB1 by aptamer and effectively triggers trans-cleavage of a pair of self-reporting single-stranded DNA-locked RNA2 fluorescence probes (named as dual-winged fluorescence probe). The released RNA2 then initiates an autocatalytic positive feedback loop, resulting in continuous probe cleavage. The CPSCN system achieves highly sensitive detection in a single-enzyme one-step process. The method exhibits excellent quantitative capability for AFB1 detection with a detection limit of 7.5 pg/mL. In real samples, the detection results of the proposed biosensor show high consistency with those obtained by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). This work not only provides a novel strategy for AFB1 detection with high sensitivity, robustness, and operational simplicity, but also offers a new insight for designing signal amplification strategies of CRISPR-based biosensors.

title: Cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot enabling ultrasensitive one-pot detection of dual miRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: Yu L, Li X, Huang L
abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical biomarkers for the early diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but sensitive simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs remains a clinical challenge. Herein, we report an innovative biosensing method based on a cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot for one-pot, rapid, and ultrasensitive dual miRNA detection. Target miRNAs trigger the cascade DNA walker, which integrates catalytic hairpin assembly and enzyme-mediated strand displacement, to generate abundant single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). These ssDNA then activate the photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot under light illumination, enabling amplified fluorescence signaling for dual-target quantification. The assay exhibits a linear range of 100 aM to 1 pM with a limit of detection of 48.7 aM. Serum recovery experiments and cell line tests confirm its reliability in complex matrices. Clinical validation using 30 plasma samples (15 TNBC patients, 15 healthy controls) demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, AUC = 0.964). This method features simple operation and strong clinical translational potential, offering a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of TNBC.

title: Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.
authors: Guo H, Jiang Y, Li D, He K, Chen Y, Li Y, Dai S, He Y
abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a major pathogen responsible for adverse perinatal outcomes; rapid and accurate detection is crucial for preventing maternal-neonatal transmission and for guiding clinical interventions. Current GBS detection methods are limited by long assay times, insufficient sensitivity, and high equipment and operational requirements, restricting their application in resource-limited settings and rapid detection scenarios. Targeting the cfb gene of GBS, this study developed ERA-CasMNPs by integrating enzymatic recombinase amplification (ERA), CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated specific recognition and trans-cleavage activity of ssDNA, and horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-modified magnetic nanoparticle complexes (MNPs)-based colorimetric signal output. The ERA-CasMNPs biosensor enables rapid and sensitive visual detection of GBS within 85 min, with an LOD95 of 23.3 copies/μL (95% confidence interval: 15.6-34.8 copies/μL). Moreover, evaluation using 135 cultured clinical bacterial isolates demonstrated that ERA-CasMNPs achieved a sensitivity of 97.33%, a specificity of 98.33%, and a detection accuracy of 97.78%, comparable to qPCR. These results indicate that the ERA-CasMNPs biosensor provides a sensitive and visual method for rapid detection of GBS and supports its potential for further evaluation in resource-limited and rapid-testing settings.

title: Magnoflorine alleviates depression-like behaviors via modulation of serotonergic signaling and neurotrophic pathways.
authors: Zhao Y, Gong Y, Li H, Ren L, Zhao X, Chen Z
abstract: Depression is a prevalent and debilitating psychiatric disorder characterized by dysregulation of monoaminergic neurotransmission and impaired neuroplasticity, and current antidepressants are limited by delayed onset and suboptimal efficacy, necessitating novel multi-target therapeutics. Magnoflorine, an alkaloid derived from Ziziphi Spinosae Semen (Suanzaoren), has been reported to possess antianxiety and neuroprotective activities, but its antidepressant effects and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study employed an integrated strategy combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation to investigate the antidepressant effects of magnoflorine. The effects of magnoflorine were evaluated in corticosterone (CORT)-induced HT-22 cells and a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model using behavioral tests, neurochemical analysis, histological analysis, and Western blotting. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that magnoflorine may regulate multiple targets involved in depression, particularly serotonergic signaling pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested potential interactions between magnoflorine and 5-HT1AR/SERT. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that magnoflorine ameliorated CORT-induced neuronal injury and CUMS-associated depression-like behaviors, restored hippocampal monoamine levels, and alleviated neuronal damage. These effects were accompanied by alterations in 5-HT1AR and SERT expression and enhanced ERK phosphorylation and BDNF expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that the antidepressant-like effects of magnoflorine are associated with modulation of serotonergic and neurotrophic signaling.

title: Identification of neoechinulin B metabolites in vivo by UPLC Q/TOF MS and exploration of its anti HCV mechanism based on network pharmacology and molecular docking.
authors: Ren X, Lu XH, Chen YF, Tu XP, Li BY, Tao X, Yang X, Zhang FX
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: Fungal secondary metabolites, owing to their structural diversity and broad spectrum of bioactivities, have become a vital source for the discovery of microbial drugs and antiviral lead compounds. Fungi of the genus Aspergillus, which are ubiquitous filamentous microorganisms, are capable of producing structurally novel and functionally diverse secondary metabolites, thus representing a rich reservoir for drug lead discovery. Neoechinulin B (NeoB), an isoprenyl indole diketopiperazine alkaloid isolated from Aspergillus strains, exhibits potent antiviral activity. However, its poor characterization in terms of in vivo metabolism has hindered further development. In this work, we systematically explored the metabolic profile of NeoB in Sprague-Dawley rats, and combined network pharmacology with molecular docking to generate hypotheses regarding its potential anti‑HCV mechanism. These computational results are predictive and require future experimental validation. Following oral administration of NeoB to rats at 20 mg/kg/day, a total of 18 compounds, including NeoB and its metabolites, were identified in plasma, urine, faeces, heart, and liver. The proposed major metabolic pathways involved demethylation, sulfation, and glucuronidation. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were then used to generate hypotheses regarding potential anti-HCV targets. These computational results are predictive and require future experimental validation. Network pharmacology suggested that NeoB and its representative metabolites may potentially modulate targets such as SRC and EGFR, and by interfering with signalling pathways including "Proteoglycans in cancer" and "Hepatitis C". Molecular docking results suggested a potential preference for SRC over EGFR based on docking scores. However, because redocking validation for EGFR and SRC did not meets the 2.0 Å threshold, theses docking scores are considered computational estimates only. They cannot be used to infer target selectivity or differences in binding affinity. The parent compound P0 showed lowest docking score with SRC (-10.5 kcal/mol)), but this value is a computational estimate and does not represent experimental binding affinity. Overall, the docking outcomes were consistent with the network pharmacology predictions. This study qualitatively characterizes the in vivo metabolic profile of NeoB and provides computational hypotheses for future research. Any therapeutic implications remain speculative.

title: Rare-earth-free magnesium-zinc alloy with controlled biodegradation and biocompatibility for novel biodegradable metallic stent.
authors: Park Y, Ha Y, Roh HJ, Lee H, Eo SJ, Kang DY, Lee N, Jung HD
abstract: Biodegradable magnesium (Mg) alloy stents offer a transient alternative to permanent metallic implants; however, clinically used WE43 contains rare-earth (RE) elements, raising concerns regarding the long-term biosafety of RE-containing degradation products and their potential tissue accumulation. Here, we investigated two RE-free Mg-Zinc (Zn)-based alloys, MZ01 (Mg-1Zn-0.1Ca) and ZM115 (Mg-1Zn-1.5Mn-0.5Sr), and established a mechanistic cascade linking alloy composition and microstructure to electrochemical analyses revealed alloy-dependent differences in grain structure and interfacial corrosion resistance, with MZ01 exhibiting the highest charge-transfer resistance. In a mouse subcutaneous model, MZ01 showed more uniform degradation, smaller and more rapidly resolving hydrogen gas cavities, and a significantly lower microcrack area fraction at Day 56 than WE43 and ZM115, accompanied by attenuated inflammatory and fibrotic responses. In the rabbit iliac arteries, all stents maintained luminal patency without thrombosis through 56 days, while MZ01 exhibited lower neointimal thickness, lower perivascular apoptosis and late inflammation, and enhanced early endothelialization compared with WE43. Preliminary descriptive porcine coronary implantation further demonstrated the technical feasibility and sustained patency of MZ01 over 56 days. Collectively, these findings define a composition-microstructure-corrosion-cellular response-vascular healing axis and identify MZ01 as a RE-free Mg-Zn alloy with controlled biodegradation and favorable biocompatibility, supporting its further development as a biodegradable cardiovascular scaffold.

title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
authors: Liu Z, Li R, Huang W, Zhang J, Qu Y, Dong W, Liu Y, Li Q
abstract: PURPOSE: Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair. METHODS: Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA. RESULTS: We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+). CONCLUSIONS: Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
authors: Kučera J, Makarová M, Vít M, Novák J, Zlámal F, Ráčková L, Fialová Kučerová J, Grulichová M
abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals (n = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel (n = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance (r = 0.75, p = 4 × 10-9) and training status (r = 0.71, p = 6 × 10-8), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass (r = 0.57, p = 8 × 10-5). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism.
authors: Ahamba IS, Song G, Kinkpe L, Duan Q, Goswami N, Jin Z, Wu J, Dong X
abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) significantly influences meat quality, affecting flavor, tenderness, and juiciness. Despite extensive research on livestock such as cattle and pigs, the regulation of IMF in rabbits remains poorly understood. This study establishes a standardized in vitro method for isolating and characterizing intramuscular preadipocytes from the longissimus dorsi muscle of 3-day-old Hycole rabbits using enzymatic digestion and differential centrifugation. Three-day-old neonates were selected for initial protocol development due to their higher progenitor cell abundance and tissue accessibility, which facilitates method optimization and ensures consistent cell yields. Isolated cells displayed typical preadipocyte morphology and expressed key markers, including PREF-1, PPARγ, and Leptin, confirmed by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. Upon adipogenic induction, cells exhibited progressive lipid accumulation, as indicated by Oil Red O staining, and showed upregulated expression of PPARG, C/EBPa, and FABP4, confirming their differentiation potential. This study establishes a comprehensive protocol for isolating rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes, providing a foundational tool for investigating the molecular mechanisms of adipogenesis in lagomorphs. The model supports future studies on genetic and nutritional strategies to enhance rabbit meat quality while preserving its lean characteristics.

title: Prototype-Guided Test-Time Adaptation for Real-Time EMG-Based Gesture Recognition.
authors: Ma Y, Wang Y, Dai C, Guo Y
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) signals facilitate intuitive human-machine interaction and are widely employed in applications such as prosthetics and rehabilitation. However, sEMG signal distributions are highly sensitive to variations in electrode placement, user physiology, and session conditions, which significantly hinder model generalization in real-world settings. To address this, we propose EMG-based structure-aware test-time adaptive refinement (EMG-STAR), a test-time adaptation (TTA) framework tailored for online deployment without access to target data during training. EMG-STAR improves model stability by fusing historical and batch-wise normalization statistics from both source and target domains, effectively alleviating domain shifts. Furthermore, it refines predictions using a prototype-assisted feature clustering method that enforces consistency among semantically similar target samples. To further enhance reliability, the framework jointly leverages prediction confidence and distributional alignment to filter out noisy pseudo-labels during adaptation. Comprehensive evaluations conducted on two public datasets, Hyser, and NinaPro-DB2, demonstrate that EMG-STAR consistently outperforms ten existing TTA methods. Interpretability analysis using Grad-CAM reveals that EMG-STAR predominantly attends to physiologically meaningful muscle activation regions, suggesting that the model captures neuromuscular structures rather than transient signal noise.

title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Zhu J, Zhong Y, Yan S, Zeng X
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo, FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

title: Coacervate protocells-mediated mitochondrial transplantation restores gut epithelial energetic homeostasis in ulcerative colitis.
authors: Ding B, Chen Y, Jia Y, Li J, Tan Z, Wu W, Ouyang S, Tong B
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction in intestinal epithelial cells, yet current therapies fail to correct underlying energy metabolism defects. While exogenous mitochondrial transplantation offers a promising strategy, its clinical translation is hindered by rapid loss of mitochondrial bioactivity ex vivo, poor delivery efficiency, and lysosomal degradation following cellular uptake. Here, we developed a biomimetic coacervate-based protocell system (HTP) via liquid-liquid phase separation of polyethylene glycol, tannic acid, and sodium hyaluronate for efficient encapsulation and delivery of functional mitochondria (HTP@Mito). HTP protocells preserved mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis capacity for up to 72 h in HBSS buffer at 37°C, far exceeding the viability of free mitochondria. Notably, HTP markedly enhanced intracellular delivery of isolated mitochondria via lipid-raft-mediated endocytosis. In a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine UC model, rectally administrating HTP@Mito achieved superior therapeutic efficacy via restoring ATP levels and mitochondrial membrane potential, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Furthermore, by reducing oxidative stress, HTP@Mito rescued lysosomal function and restored impaired autophagic flux, thereby promoting mitophagy to clear damaged mitochondria. HTP@Mito treatment also repaired intestinal epithelial tight junctions, restored goblet cell-derived mucus secretion, and rebalanced gut microbiota by increasing beneficial Lachnospiraceae while reducing pathogenic Escherichia-Shigella. Collectively, this work established a versatile, biomimetic organelle delivery platform that could correct mitochondrial energy deficiency in the intestinal epithelium, providing a framework for mitochondrial transplantation in ulcerative colitis.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
authors: Su W, Zhang X, Li R, Li K, Guo X, Liu X, Wang Z, Wang H
abstract: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Integrated UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS, network pharmacology, and in vivo evaluation reveal bioactive constituents and mechanisms of Bushen Tongluo Decoction against idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
authors: Li K, Huang G, Ye Q, Cui H, Miao Q, Ren P
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: The active constituents and mechanisms of Bushen Tongluo Decoction (BTD) in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remain unclear. We profiled BTD constituents and serum compounds by ultra‑high‑performance liquid chromatography‑quadrupole‑Orbitrap high‑resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS) and combined network pharmacology, in vivo evaluation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis to identify candidate bioactive compounds and associated mechanisms.We identified 614 constituents in BTD and 100 serum compounds, including 50 prototype compounds and 50 metabolites; 32 met Level 1 identification criteria. Network pharmacology identified 171 shared targets and prioritized transforming growth factor‑beta (TGF-β)- and mitogen‑activated protein kinase (MAPK)-related pathways. BTD reduced histopathological injury, collagen accumulation, and α‑smooth muscle actin (α‑SMA) and fibronectin 1 (FN1) expression, with stronger effects at the higher dose. Treatment was associated with changes in TGF-β1, Smad2/3, extracellular signal‑regulated kinase (ERK), and their phosphorylated forms. Ellagic acid showed the most favorable predicted binding energy at the latency-associated peptide (LAP)- growth factor (GF) interface of TGF-β1. MD analyses supported relative complex stability and yielded an estimated binding free energy of -59.43 ± 4.79 kJ/mol. SPR analysis detected binding between ellagic acid and TGF-β1, yielding a KD of 3.63 × 10⁻⁶ M. These findings indicate that BTD attenuated experimental pulmonary fibrosis and nominate ellagic acid as a candidate active constituent, and support the involvement of TGF-β1/Smads/ERK-related signaling in its effects on experimental pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Pharmacokinetic comparison of 18 constituents from Qingxin Zishen Prescription in normal and ovariectomized rats via a validated HPLC-MS/MS method.
authors: Xie K, Sui J, Hu Y, Li Y, Chen J, Sun H, Liu L, Zhu K
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: Qingxin Zishen Prescription (QZP) is an empirical formula for treating menopausal syndrome, yet the pharmacokinetic behavior of its constituents under pathological conditions remains poorly understood. In the present work, we developed and validated a sensitive high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) method to simultaneously quantify 18 representative bioactive constituents of QZP in rat plasma, and applied it to a comparative pharmacokinetic study in normal and ovariectomized (OVX) rats. Sample preparation involved protein precipitation with acetonitrile followed by concentration. Separation was achieved on an Agilent ZORBAX SB C18 column (4.6 ×100 mm, 1.8 μm), and detection was performed on a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer in both positive and negative modes. The method showed excellent linearity (r > 0.9965) with lower limits of quantification ranging from 0.015 to 25 ng/mL. The within-run and between-run precision (relative standard deviation, RSD) were within 8.58% and 10.37%, respectively, and the accuracy ranged from 85% to 115% at all quality control levels. Matrix effects ranged from 1.98% to 14.57% (RSD), and extraction recoveries ranged from 85.54% to 113.29%, both within acceptable limits. Stability under different storage conditions was also verified. The comparative pharmacokinetic study revealed that the t1/2 of rhynchophylline, corynoxeine, hirsuteine, magnoflorine, and catalpol were significantly prolonged in OVX rats, whereas that of demethyleneberberine was significantly shortened. In addition, hirsuteine showed significantly increased Cmax and AUC0-t, suggesting enhanced absorption in the pathological state. The results clarify the systemic exposure behavior of the main bioactive components of QZP and highlight marked pharmacokinetic differences between healthy and OVX rats. These findings indicate that estrogen deficiency significantly modulates the elimination and systemic exposure of multiple QZP constituents, suggesting that dose adjustment may be necessary when administering herbal medicines to menopausal patients.

title: Microfluidic integrated nucleic acid test (MINT) enabled by coupling FEN1-aided RPA with wax-purification and bead-carrier.
authors: Xu Z, Gao X, Huang J, Pang S, Wang S, Wang Y, Feng L, Ma Y
abstract: To guide timely antibiotic treatment, a tool for quick antimicrobial resistance gene detection is required. Here a Microfluidic Integrated Nucleic Acid Test platform (namely, MINT) was proposed for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. The platform integrates fast nucleic acid extraction based on hybrid wax-phase purification, and DNA amplification based on our newly developed FEN1-aided RPA (FARPA) into a microfluidic chip. The wax-phase stays solid at room temperature, while becomes liquid at >50 °C to allow the wash of inhibitors carried from extraction buffer, thus the chip keeps stable during storage and transportation. The movement of extracted DNA bound with magnetic beads were controlled by a magnet. The beaded DNA was quickly purified during the flow through the wax phase, and the amplification started once the beaded DNA reached to the well for FARPA. The signal from target-positive sample could be readily sensed by a conventional smartphone. The turnaround time is about 40 min from the sample to the result. The platform was validated by detecting the blaKPC-2 resistance gene of Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) from urine samples with the reliable detection concentration of 500 CFU/mL, achieving 100% agreement for the 29 clinical urine samples (19 positive, 10 negative) with conventional qPCR. It is easy to adapt the MINT to any other pathogen only by designing the corresponding primers and probes for FARPA. It is promising to apply MINT for bed-site antimicrobial resistance screening just after operation.

title: Decoding bacterial identity and resistance through D-amino acid metabolic fingerprinting with a cascade colorimetric sensor array.
authors: Yang X, Yang D, Sun W, Song Y, Yang B, Huang P, Liu J, Gao X
abstract: The rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) constitutes a global health crisis, demanding diagnostic tools capable of simultaneous bacterial identification and rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing (AST) in a single workflow. Herein, a colorimetric sensor array was developed to address this need by profiling bacterial metabolic fingerprints via a streamlined single-substrate, multi-wavelength strategy. The strategy is built upon the inherent bacteria-specific metabolism of D-amino acids (D-AAs), coupled with the enzymatic selectivity of D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO), which catalyzes the oxidation of D-AAs to generate H2O2. Differential bacterial consumption of D-Ala directly modulates the substrate available for the subsequent DAAO-coupled cascade reaction, producing varying amounts of H2O2. Consequently, H2O2 triggers the peroxidase (POD)-like activity of Prussian blue-coated gold nanoparticle (Au@PB NP) nanozyme to produce distinct multi-wavelength optical patterns from TMB oxidation. When coupled with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), this sensing platform enables clear discrimination of bacterial species based on their metabolic fingerprints. Moreover, by assessing the antibiotic-induced inhibition of this metabolic activity, the platform accurately determines bacterial susceptibility profiles, achieving 100% concordance with the standard disk diffusion method for both reference and clinical isolates, and successfully determining minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values for reference strains in full agreement with Clinical Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) breakpoint interpretation. This work establishes an integrated, rapid, and robust metabolic sensing platform for bacterial phenotyping and AST, offering a promising tool to combat AMR.

title: Integrated profiling of β-lactam susceptibility and spoilage-associated enzyme activities in psychrotrophic bacteria from the raw milk production chain.
authors: Hu X, Lei Y, Kong Z, Pang X, Shen J, Wang S
abstract: Psychrotrophic bacteria are important targets for microbiological control of cold-chain raw milk because of their ability to produce spoilage-associated enzymes and harbor antimicrobial resistance determinants. However, these two functional characteristics are often investigated separately, leaving their co-occurrence within the same isolate collection insufficiently characterized. To address this gap, 543 dominant culturable bacterial isolates were recovered from raw milk and dairy-farm-associated samples collected from six regions of China. Pseudomonas was the most prevalent genus, followed by Acinetobacter, Chryseobacterium, Serratia, and Psychrobacter. β-Lactam minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) distributions varied substantially among genera, with Chryseobacterium exhibiting the highest proportion of β-lactamase-associated phenotype-positive isolates. Among 226 raw-milk isolates screened using ceftazidime, all 44 isolates showing inhibitor-responsive or carbapenemase-associated phenotypes were subjected to whole-genome sequencing. Genome-wide resistance-gene screening identified annotated β-lactamase genes predominantly in Chryseobacterium and Acinetobacter. In contrast, the resistance-related annotations retained in phenotype-positive Pseudomonas isolates were mainly associated with efflux systems and adaptive response mechanisms. In the integrated analysis, a relative MIC-enzyme risk-prioritization score ranked Serratia (0.88), Chryseobacterium (0.71), and Pseudomonas (0.67) as the three highest-ranking genera. The β-lactam MIC score showed weak positive correlations with the protease-associated score (Spearman's ρ = 0.297, P < 0.001) and with the lipase-associated score (ρ = 0.194, P < 0.001). These findings indicate that genus abundance alone is insufficient to characterize the functional heterogeneity of psychrotrophic bacteria in raw milk. Integrating β-lactam MIC patterns with spoilage-enzyme activity provides complementary information for genus-level prioritization within this isolate collection.

title: Sensitive detection of 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal-modified proteins in oxidative stress-related diseases.
authors: Méndez-Cuadro D, Kamali AN, Ruiz C, Pérez-Benavente S, Hernáez ML, Rodríguez-Cavallo E, Puyet A, Bautista JM
abstract: Protein modification by 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (HNE) is associated with metabolic, neurodegenerative, and infectious diseases characterized by oxidative stress. Detecting low-abundance HNE-protein adducts in complex extracts requires antibodies with suitable reactivity and selectivity. We generated polyclonal antisera in rabbits using matched-species rabbit serum albumin modified in vitro with HNE (RSA-HNE), administered either intact or after tryptic digestion. The antisera displayed distinct recognition profiles across dot blot, ELISA, and Western blot assays using HNE-modified standards and membrane-protein extracts from uninfected and Plasmodium falciparum-infected human erythrocytes. Antiserum 1, raised against intact RSA-HNE, showed the stronger overall immunochemical response, whereas Antiserum 2, raised against tryptic RSA-HNE, displayed a different and more restricted peptide-recognition profile. In an immunoenrichment and LC-MS/MS workflow, Antiserum 1 recovered 14 candidate HNE-associated membrane proteins from erythrocytes infected with P. falciparum trophozoites. Site-specific evidence remained tentative for four peptides. These antisera are therefore proposed as research tools for studying protein lipoxidation, although biological replication and orthogonal validation of the candidate modification sites are required.

title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
authors: Höiby P, Zarrouk M, Lind L, Basna R, Overton MC, Elmståhl S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Biomimetic sequential targeted nanoplatform for synergistic thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
authors: Wang J, Wang X, Liu S, Zheng Y, Wang C, Cheng J, Wang X
abstract: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.
